mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.0% over three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes corporate earnings slowdowns and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises above 5.0% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE has been above 5.0% for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a weakening housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader consumer demand slowdown; this combination predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both RSAFS and HOUST decline for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO below 100 for two consecutive months), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to reduced corporate output and profit margins; this effect is most pronounced in the early stages of a manufacturing slowdown over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO has been below 100 for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer spending trend, as measured by residential fixed investment (RSAFS), indicates strong household demand which supports corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS is rising, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL annual inflation rate exceeds 2.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a tight labor market that fuels wage pressures and inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the Fed may tighten policy.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS grows and UNRATE declines for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of active monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS above 1.0%), the S&P 500 tends to experience negative returns due to higher discount rates and reduced corporate borrowing; this effect is most pronounced during the initial phase of a rate hike cycle over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 1.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.
